question: In primary angle-closure glaucoma (PACG), aqueous humour accumulates behind the iris due to pupil block — the relative obstruction between the posterior iris surface and the anterior lens — causing anterior bowing of the peripheral iris that occludes the trabecular meshwork.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. The pupil block mechanism — posterior iris pressed against the anterior lens capsule — is central to PACG. This is entirely different from POAG, where the angle remains open but trabecular resistance increases gradually.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Pupil block is the hallmark mechanism. Aqueous cannot pass through the pupil normally, pressure builds in the posterior chamber, the peripheral iris bows forward (iris bombé), and closes the iridocorneal angle — trapping aqueous and acutely elevating IOP.
